join_order.notes: Single k_id; CSR slot yields mk rows (likely 1e4-1e5).
Keyword is very common -> t1_ids large; ml is tiny (~30K). Linear ml scan + hash-set probe on ml.movie_id beats per-t1 range walk because most t1 ranges are empty but |t1_ids| >> |ml|.
Dense PK direct dereference; no hash needed.

data_structures.aggregation: three_running_mins (lt.link as string_view, t1.title as string_view, t2.title as string_view)

morsel_targets: keyword scan (134170 rows, single thread acceptable; 12-way split optional)
movie_link linear scan (29,997 rows, split into morsels of ~2500 rows across 12 threads)
MIN aggregation reduced via thread-local mins then global reduce on string_view (compare bytes)
parallelism.notes: Building t1_ids: single-threaded build over CSR slice is fine (slot size << shared-set overhead). If slot very large (>500K), use 12 thread-local sets then merge.

indexes.purpose: direct slot lookup for k_id -> mk rowids
direct dereference for t1.title and t2.title

notes_for_codegen: Resolve k_id by single scan of keyword/keyword.{off,dat}; break on first match (keyword is unique).
Build t1_ids by iterating CSR rowids[offsets[k_id]..offsets[k_id+1]) and inserting mk.movie_id[r] into hash set.

Also track MIN(t1.title) during this phase OR defer to after ml filter; defer is wrong (t1 must satisfy ml join too). Since join is INNER on ml, MIN(t1.title) is taken over t1_ids that appear as ml.movie_id. Compute during the ml linear scan: if t1_ids.contains(ml.movie_id[r]), update min_t1 with title[ml.movie_id[r]-1].
For each surviving ml row: update min_lt with link_type.link[ml.link_type_id[r]-1], update min_t2 with title[ml.linked_movie_id[r]-1].
String MIN: lexicographic byte compare on the varlen payload via offsets.
No NULL handling needed (all joins are equi-joins with non-null keys).
